In the following, we use Borel-Moore homology (with coefficient $A$). 
For simplicity of notations, we only write them as $H_i(\cdot, A)$.
Denote by $\text{NH}_3(X, \mathbb{Z}/\ell^n)$ the group $N^{d-2}H_3(X, \mathbb{Z}/\ell^n)$.



Given an equi-dimensional family of one-cycles $\Gamma_S$ over a smooth projective variety $S$, we have a commutative diagram
\begin{equation}\label{eq:cd1}
\xymatrix{
 CH_0(S,1, \mathbb{Z}/\ell^n) \ar[r]^{ \Gamma_{S*}}\ar[d]^{ \Gamma_{S*}\circ cl^S_{1, 1}} &\text{CH}_1(X, 1, \mathbb{Z}/\ell^n) \ar@{->>}[r]\ar[d]^{cl_{1, 1}^X} &A_1(X)[\ell^n] \ar[d]^{cl_{1}}\\
   H_3(X, \mathbb{Z}/\ell^n)  \ar[r]^= & H_3(X, \mathbb{Z}/\ell^n) \ar[r] & H_2(X, \mathbb{Z}_\ell)[\ell^n]}.
\end{equation}

The left vertical map is the composition of cycle class map $cl^S_{1, 1}$ for $S$ and action of the correspondence $\Gamma_S$ on cohomology.
The middle and the right vertical maps are (higher) cycle class maps. 

The left square is commutative by Proposition \ref{class_cor}. The right square is commutative by Proposition \ref{prop:bockstein} and the fact that cycle class map is trivial on cycles that are algebraically equivalent to $0$.

The first observation is that the image of left and middle vertical maps actually lands in a smaller group.

\begin{claim}\label{claim:mid}
    The image of the higher cycle class map
\[
cl_{1, 1}^X: \text{CH}_1(X, 1, \mathbb{Z}/\ell^n) \to H_3(X, \mathbb{Z}/\ell^n)
\]
is $\text{NH}_3(X, \mathbb{Z}/\ell^n)\subset H_3(X, \mathbb{Z}/\ell^n)$.
\end{claim}
\begin{proof}
We first note that \[
cl_{1, 1}^X: \text{CH}_1(X, 1, \mathbb{Z}/\ell^n) \to H_3(X, \mathbb{Z}/\ell^n)
\]
factors through $\text{NH}_3(X, \mathbb{Z}/\ell^n)\subset H_3(X, \mathbb{Z}/\ell^n)$.
This is because any element in $\text{CH}_1(X, 1, \mathbb{Z}/\ell^n)$ is represented by a family of  one-cycles over $\Delta^1\cong \mathbb{A}^1$, and thus comes from $\text{CH}_1(\Sigma, 1, \mathbb{Z}/\ell^n)$ for some surface $\Sigma$ (which can be taken as the closure in $X$ of the locus swept out by the support of this family of one-cycles over $\Delta^1$). Therefore the higher cycle class map factors through $\text{NH}_3(X, \mathbb{Z}/\ell^n)$ by the functoriality of higher cycle class maps under proper push-forward (Proposition \ref{prop:func}).

Since the higher cycle class map is compatible with proper push-forward (Proposition \ref{prop:func}), we have a commutative diagram 
\[
\begin{CD}
    \oplus_\Sigma \text{CH}_1(\Sigma, 1, \mathbb{Z}/\ell^n) @>cl_{1,1}^\Sigma>\cong> \oplus_\Sigma H_3(\Sigma, \mathbb{Z}/\ell^n)\\
    @VVV @VVV\\
    \text{CH}_1(X, 1, \mathbb{Z}/\ell^n) @>cl_{1, 1}^X>> \text{NH}_3(X, \mathbb{Z}/\ell^n),
\end{CD}
\]
where the direct sum is over all $2$-dimensional finite type connected reduced schemes $\Sigma$ with a proper morphism to $X$.
In the commutative diagram,
the upper horizontal arrow is an isomorphism induced by the higher cycle class map (Lemma \ref{lem:surface_CH_1_1}),
and the right vertical arrow is surjective by the definition of $\text{NH}_3(X, \mathbb{Z}/\ell^n)$. Therefore the map
\[
\text{CH}_1(X, 1, \mathbb{Z}/\ell^n) \to \text{NH}_3(X,\mathbb{Z}/\ell^n)
\]
is surjective.
\end{proof}
\begin{claim}\label{claim:left1}
The map 
\[
\Gamma_{S*}\circ cl^S_{1, 1}: CH_0(S, 1, \mathbb{Z}/\ell^n) \to H_3(X, \mathbb{Z}/\ell^n)
\]
factors through $H_3(X, \mathbb{Z}_\ell)/\ell^n \subset H_3(X, \mathbb{Z}/\ell^n)$.
\end{claim}
\begin{proof}
 For any variety $Y$,
we have a short exact sequence
\[
0 \to H_1(Y, \mathbb{Z}_\ell)/\ell^n \to H_1(Y, \mathbb{Z}/\ell^n) \to H_0(Y, \mathbb{Z}_\ell)[\ell^n] \to 0.
\]
Therefore $H_1(Y, \mathbb{Z}_\ell)/\ell^n \xrightarrow{\cong} H_1(Y, \mathbb{Z}/\ell^n)$,
since $H_0(Y, \mathbb{Z}_\ell)\xrightarrow{\cong} \mathbb{Z}_\ell$ is torsion free.

The cycle class map induces an isomorphism (Corollary \ref{cor:ch_BM})$$cl_{0, 1}:CH_0(S,1, \mathbb{Z}/\ell^n) \xrightarrow{\cong} H_1(S, \mathbb{Z}/\ell^n)\xrightarrow{\cong} H_1(S, \mathbb{Z}_\ell)/\ell^n.$$

This fact, combined with the following commutative diagram:
\[
\begin{CD}
    H_1(S, \mathbb{Z}_\ell)@>\mod \ell^n >> H_1(S, \mathbb{Z}_\ell)/\ell^n @>\cong >> H_1(S, \mathbb{Z}/\ell^n)\\
    @VV\Gamma_{S*}V @VV\Gamma_{S*}V @VV\Gamma_{S*} V\\
    H_3(X, \mathbb{Z}_\ell)@>\mod \ell^n>> H_3(X, \mathbb{Z}_\ell)/\ell^n @>>> H_3(X, \mathbb{Z}/\ell^n),
\end{CD}
\]
shows that the left vertical arrow in the commutative diagram (\ref{eq:cd1}) is the composition
\[
    CH_0(S, 1, \mathbb{Z}/\ell^n) \xrightarrow{\cong} H_1(S, \mathbb{Z}/\ell^n)\cong H_1(S, \mathbb{Z}_\ell)/\ell^n \xrightarrow{\Gamma_{S*}} H_3(X, \mathbb{Z}_\ell)/\ell^n\to H_3(X, \mathbb{Z}/\ell^n).
\]
This proves the claim.
\end{proof}

Furthermore, the image of
\[
\Gamma_{S*}\circ cl^S_{1, 1}: CH_0(S, 1, \mathbb{Z}/\ell^n) \to H_3(X, \mathbb{Z}/\ell^n)
\]
is also contained in $\text{NH}_3(X, \mathbb{Z}/\ell^n)$ since the middle vertical map has image contained in it (Claim \ref{claim:mid}).
So we have an induced commutative diagram:
\begin{equation}\label{eq:cd}
\xymatrix{
\oplus_{(S, \Gamma_S)} CH_0(S,1, \mathbb{Z}/\ell^n)\ar[r]^{\oplus \Gamma_{S*}}\ar[d]^{\oplus \Gamma_{S*}\circ cl_{1, 1}^S} &\text{CH}_1(X, 1, \mathbb{Z}/\ell^n) \ar@{->>}[r]\ar[d]^{cl_{1, 1}^X} &A_1(X)[\ell^n] \ar[d]^{cl_{1}} \to 0\\
  0 \to H_3(X, \mathbb{Z}_\ell)/\ell^n \cap \text{NH}_3(X, \mathbb{Z}/\ell^n) \ar@{^{(}->}[r] & \text{NH}_3(X, \mathbb{Z}/\ell^n) \ar[r] & H_2(X, \mathbb{Z}_\ell)[\ell^n]},
\end{equation}
where the direct sum is taken over isomorphism classes of equi-dimensional families of one-cycles over smooth projective varieties. 

By Theorem \ref{thm:sheaf_surj}, the upper row is exact. The lower row is also exact, since it comes from
\[
0 \to H_3(X, \mathbb{Z}_\ell)/\ell^n \to H_3(X, \mathbb{Z}/\ell^n) \to H_2(X, \mathbb{Z}_\ell)[\ell^n] \to 0.
\]

We can be even more precise about the image of the left vertical map.
\begin{claim}\label{claim:left}
    The image of the left vertical map in the commutative diagram (\ref{eq:cd}) equals the image of $\tilde{N}H_3(X, \mathbb{Z}_\ell)/\ell^n \to H_3(X, \mathbb{Z}_\ell)/\ell^n \cap \text{NH}_3(X, \mathbb{Z}/\ell^n)$.
\end{claim}
\begin{proof}[Proof of Claim \ref{claim:left}]
   By the proof of Claim \ref{claim:left1}, the left vertical arrow in the commutative diagram (\ref{eq:cd}) is the direct sum of the  compositions
\[
CH_0(S, 1, \mathbb{Z}/\ell^n) \xrightarrow{\cong} H_1(S, \mathbb{Z}/\ell^n)\cong H_1(S, \mathbb{Z}_\ell)/\ell^n \xrightarrow{\Gamma_{S*}} H_3(X, \mathbb{Z}_\ell)/\ell^n.\]


Therefore, by Lemma \ref{cyl_equiv}, the left vertical map in the commutative diagram (\ref{eq:cd}) has the same image as $$\tilde{N}_{1, \text{cyl}}H_3(X, \mathbb{Z}_\ell)/\ell^n \to H_3(X, \mathbb{Z}_\ell)/\ell^n \cap \text{NH}_3(X, \mathbb{Z}/\ell^n).$$
 By Lemma \ref{lem:inclusion}, $\tilde{N}_{1, \text{cyl}}H_3(X, \mathbb{Z}_\ell)=\tilde{N}^{d-2}H_3(X, \mathbb{Z}_\ell)$. This proves the claim.
\end{proof}

Note that $\tilde{N}H_3(X, \mathbb{Z}_\ell)\subset \text{NH}_3(X, \mathbb{Z}_\ell)\subset H_3(X, \mathbb{Z}_\ell)$ are finitely generated $\mathbb{Z}_\ell$-modules. Thus we have isomorphisms 
\[
\tilde{N}H_3(X, \mathbb{Z}_\ell) \xrightarrow{\cong}\lim \limits_{\xleftarrow[n]{}} \tilde{N}H_3(X, \mathbb{Z}_\ell)/\ell^n,\quad
 \text{NH}_3(X, \mathbb{Z}_\ell) \xrightarrow{\cong}
\lim \limits_{\xleftarrow[n]{}} \text{NH}_3(X, \mathbb{Z}_\ell)/\ell^n.
\]

We have a factorization
\[
\tilde{N}H_3(X, \mathbb{Z}_\ell)/\ell^n \to {N}H_3(X, \mathbb{Z}_\ell)/\ell^n \to H_3(X, \mathbb{Z}_\ell)/\ell^n \cap \text{NH}_3(X, \mathbb{Z}/\ell^n) \subset H_3(X, \mathbb{Z}_\ell)/\ell^n.
\]
Taking inverse limit, we get maps
\begin{equation*}
    \tilde{N}H_3(X, \mathbb{Z}_\ell) \to \text{NH}_3(X, \mathbb{Z}_\ell) \to \lim \limits_{\xleftarrow[n]{}} (H_3(X, \mathbb{Z}_\ell)/\ell^n \cap \text{NH}_3(X, \mathbb{Z}/\ell^n)) \subset H_3(X, \mathbb{Z}_\ell).
\end{equation*}
Here the last inclusion is preserved due to left exactness of inverse limit.

Since the compositions
\[
\tilde{N}H_3(X, \mathbb{Z}_\ell) \to {N}H_3(X, \mathbb{Z}_\ell) \to \lim \limits_{\xleftarrow[n]{}} H_3(X, \mathbb{Z}_\ell)/\ell^n \cap \text{NH}_3(X, \mathbb{Z}/\ell^n) \to H_3(X, \mathbb{Z}_\ell)
\]
are the inclusions of subgroups, we have the following claim.
\begin{claim}\label{claim:inj}
    We have inclusions
    \[
\tilde{N}\text{H}_3(X, \mathbb{Z}_\ell) \subset \text{NH}_3(X, \mathbb{Z}_\ell) \subset \lim \limits_{\xleftarrow[n]{}} H_3(X, \mathbb{Z}_\ell)/\ell^n \cap \text{NH}_3(X, \mathbb{Z}/\ell^n) \subset H_3(X, \mathbb{Z}_\ell)
\]
\end{claim}


Now our next claim is:
\begin{claim}\label{claim:torfree}
    The cokernel of the inclusion
\begin{equation}\label{eq:torsionfree}
     \tilde{N}H_3(X, \mathbb{Z}_\ell) \to \lim \limits_{\xleftarrow[n]{}} H_3(X, \mathbb{Z}_\ell)/\ell^n \cap \text{NH}_3(X, \mathbb{Z}/\ell^n)
\end{equation}
is torsion free. 
So is the cokernel of the inclusion \[
\tilde{N}^{d-2}H_3(X, \mathbb{Z}_\ell)\to N^{d-2}H_3(X, \mathbb{Z}_\ell).\]
\end{claim}
\begin{proof}[Proof of Claim \ref{claim:torfree}]


By the snake lemma and Claims \ref{claim:mid}, \ref{claim:left}, we have an exact sequence:
\begin{equation}\label{eq:exact}
    \tilde{N}H_3(X, \mathbb{Z}_\ell)/\ell^n \to H_3(X, \mathbb{Z}_\ell)/\ell^n \cap \text{NH}_3(X, \mathbb{Z}/\ell^n) \to C_n \to 0,
\end{equation}
where 
$C_n$ is the cokernel of
\begin{equation}\label{eq:alpha}
    \alpha_n: \text{Ker}(\text{CH}_1(X, 1, \mathbb{Z}/\ell^n) \to \text{NH}_3(X, \mathbb{Z}/\ell^n)) \to \text{Ker}(A_1[\ell^n] \to H_2(X, \mathbb{Z}_\ell)[\ell^n]).
\end{equation}

Since $C_n$ is a quotient of $\text{Ker}(A_1[\ell^n] \to H_2(X, \mathbb{Z}_\ell)[\ell^n])$, the kernel of connecting maps $C_{n+m} \to C_n$ contains the $\ell^m$-torsions $C_{n+m}[\ell^m]$. 
Therefore the inverse limit $\lim \limits_{\xleftarrow[n]{}} C_n$ is torsion free. 

Every term involved in the exact sequence (\ref{eq:exact}) is a finite abelian group, and thus the exact sequence (\ref{eq:exact}) satisfies the Mittag-Leffler condition and the inverse limit of (\ref{eq:exact}) is exact. 
So the cokernel of 
\[
\lim \limits_{\xleftarrow[n]{}}\tilde{N}H_3(X, \mathbb{Z}_\ell)/\ell^n \to \lim \limits_{\xleftarrow[n]{}} H_3(X, \mathbb{Z}_\ell)/\ell^n \cap \text{NH}_3(X, \mathbb{Z}/\ell^n)
\]
is $\lim \limits_{\xleftarrow[n]{}} C_n$ and torsion free.

In view of the inclusions in Claim \ref{claim:inj}, the cokernel of $\tilde{N}H_3 \to \text{NH}_3$ is a sub-$\mathbb{Z}_\ell$-module of the cokernel of $\tilde{N}H_3(X, \mathbb{Z}_\ell) \to \lim \limits_{\xleftarrow[n]{}} H_3(X, \mathbb{Z}_\ell)/\ell^n \cap \text{NH}_3(X, \mathbb{Z}/\ell^n)$, and thus also torsion free. This proves the claim. 
\end{proof}

On the other hand, we know that the quotient $N^{d-2}H_3(X, \mathbb{Z}_\ell)/\tilde{N}^{d-2}H_3(X, \mathbb{Z}_\ell)$ is torsion since the strong coniveau filtration and coniveau filtration agree for $\mathbb{Q}_\ell$-coefficient. 
So it has to be zero. 
That is, the two subgroups coincide:
\[
\tilde{N}^{d-2}H_3(X, \mathbb{Z}_\ell)=N^{d-2}H_3(X, \mathbb{Z}_\ell).\]

\[

\]
Therefore $H_1(Y, \mathbb{Z}_\ell)/\ell^n \xrightarrow{\cong} H_1(Y, \mathbb{Z}/\ell^n)$,
since $H_0(Y, \mathbb{Z}_\ell)\xrightarrow{\cong} \mathbb{Z}_\ell$ is torsion free.

This fact, combined with the following commutative diagram:
\[
\begin{CD}
    H_1(S, \mathbb{Z}_\ell)@>\mod \ell^n >> H_1(S, \mathbb{Z}_\ell)/\ell^n @>\cong >> H_1(S, \mathbb{Z}/\ell^n)\\
    @VV\Gamma_{S*}V @VV\Gamma_{S*}V @VV\Gamma_{S*} V\\
    H_3(X, \mathbb{Z}_\ell)@>\mod \ell^n>> H_3(X, \mathbb{Z}_\ell)/\ell^n @>>> H_3(X, \mathbb{Z}/\ell^n),
\end{CD}
\]
shows that the left vertical arrow in the commutative diagram (\ref{eq:cd1}) is the composition
\[
    CH_0(S, 1, \mathbb{Z}/\ell^n) \xrightarrow{\cong} H_1(S, \mathbb{Z}/\ell^n)\cong H_1(S, \mathbb{Z}_\ell)/\ell^n \xrightarrow{\Gamma_{S*}} H_3(X, \mathbb{Z}_\ell)/\ell^n\to H_3(X, \mathbb{Z}/\ell^n).
\]
This proves the claim.

By the snake lemma and Claims \ref{claim:mid}, \ref{claim:left}, we have an exact sequence:
\begin{equation}\label{eq:exact}
    \tilde{N}H_3(X, \mathbb{Z}_\ell)/\ell^n \to H_3(X, \mathbb{Z}_\ell)/\ell^n \cap \text{NH}_3(X, \mathbb{Z}/\ell^n) \to C_n \to 0,
\end{equation}
where 
$C_n$ is the cokernel of
\begin{equation}\label{eq:alpha}
    \alpha_n: \text{Ker}(\text{CH}_1(X, 1, \mathbb{Z}/\ell^n) \to \text{NH}_3(X, \mathbb{Z}/\ell^n)) \to \text{Ker}(A_1[\ell^n] \to H_2(X, \mathbb{Z}_\ell)[\ell^n]).

Since $C_n$ is a quotient of $\text{Ker}(A_1[\ell^n] \to H_2(X, \mathbb{Z}_\ell)[\ell^n])$, the kernel of connecting maps $C_{n+m} \to C_n$ contains the $\ell^m$-torsions $C_{n+m}[\ell^m]$. 
Therefore the inverse limit $\lim \limits_{\xleftarrow[n]{}} C_n$ is torsion free. 

Every term involved in the exact sequence (\ref{eq:exact}) is a finite abelian group, and thus the exact sequence (\ref{eq:exact}) satisfies the Mittag-Leffler condition and the inverse limit of (\ref{eq:exact}) is exact. 
So the cokernel of 
\[
\lim \limits_{\xleftarrow[n]{}}\tilde{N}H_3(X, \mathbb{Z}_\ell)/\ell^n \to \lim \limits_{\xleftarrow[n]{}} H_3(X, \mathbb{Z}_\ell)/\ell^n \cap \text{NH}_3(X, \mathbb{Z}/\ell^n)
\]
is $\lim \limits_{\xleftarrow[n]{}} C_n$ and torsion free.

In view of the inclusions in Claim \ref{claim:inj}, the cokernel of $\tilde{N}H_3 \to \text{NH}_3$ is a sub-$\mathbb{Z}_\ell$-module of the cokernel of $\tilde{N}H_3(X, \mathbb{Z}_\ell) \to \lim \limits_{\xleftarrow[n]{}} H_3(X, \mathbb{Z}_\ell)/\ell^n \cap \text{NH}_3(X, \mathbb{Z}/\ell^n)$, and thus also torsion free. \[
\text{CH}_1(X, 1, \mathbb{Z}/\ell^n) \cong H^3(X, \tau^{\leq 2}R\pi_*{\mu_{\ell^n}^{\otimes 2}}),
\]
where $\pi: X_\text{\'et} \to X_\text{Zar}$ is the morphism from the \'etale site to the Zariski site and $\tau$ is the good truncation functor.

\label{cor:IHC}
Let $X$ be a smooth projective  variety of dimension $d$ defined over a finite field $\mathbb{F}_q$, that is separably rationally connected in codimension one.
Fix a prime number $\ell$ different from the characteristic of $k$. 
Assume one of the followings
\begin{enumerate}
    \item $N^{d-2}H_\text{\'et}^{2d-3}(\overline{X}, \mathbb{Z}_\ell(d-1))=H_\text{\'et}^{2d-3}(\overline{X}, \mathbb{Z}_\ell(d-1))$.
    \item The higher cycle class map induces a surjective map
\[
cl: \lim \limits_{\xleftarrow[n]{}}\text{CH}_1(\overline{X}, 1, \mathbb{Z}/\ell^n) \to H^{2d-3}_{\text{\'et}}(\overline{X}, \mathbb{Z}_\ell(d-1)).
\]

\end{enumerate}
Then every class in $H^1(\mathbb{F}_q, H^3(\overline{X}, \mathbb{Z}_\ell(d-1)))$ is the class of an algebraic cycle defined over $\mathbb{F}_q$.
In particular, this holds if $X$ has dimension $3$.

We first show that  the surjectivity of the map 
\[
cl: \lim \limits_{\xleftarrow[n]{}}\text{CH}_1(\overline{X}, 1, \mathbb{Z}/\ell^n) \to H^{2d-3}_{\text{\'et}}(\overline{X}, \mathbb{Z}_\ell(d-1))
\]
implies that $N^{d-2}H_\text{\'et}^{2d-3}(\overline{X}, \mathbb{Z}_\ell(d-1))=H_\text{\'et}^{2d-3}(\overline{X}, \mathbb{Z}_\ell(d-1))$.
In fact, we have a factorization of the above map
\begin{align*}
    & \lim \limits_{\xleftarrow[n]{}}\text{CH}_1(\overline{X}, 1, \mathbb{Z}/\ell^n) \to \lim \limits_{\xleftarrow[n]{}} N^{d-2}H_\text{\'et}^{2d-3}(\overline{X}, \mathbb{Z}/\ell^n(d-1))\\
    \to & \lim \limits_{\xleftarrow[n]{}}H^{2d-3}_\text{\'et}(\overline{X}, \mathbb{Z}/\ell^n(d-1))= H^{2d-3}_{\text{\'et}}(\overline{X}, \mathbb{Z}_\ell(d-1)).
\end{align*}

Therefore the map
$\lim \limits_{\xleftarrow[n]{}} N^{d-2}H_\text{\'et}^{2d-3}(\overline{X}, \mathbb{Z}/\ell^n(d-1)) \to \lim \limits_{\xleftarrow[n]{}}H^{2d-3}_\text{\'et}(\overline{X}, \mathbb{Z}/\ell^n(d-1))$
is surjective. On the other hand, since $N^{d-2}H_\text{\'et}^{2d-3}(X, \mathbb{Z}/\ell^n)$ is a subgroup of $H_\text{\'et}^{2d-3}(X, \mathbb{Z}/\ell^n)$, the inverse limit is injective, hence an isomorphism.
We have an exact sequence
\begin{align*}
 & 0 \to \lim \limits_{\xleftarrow[n]{}} H_\text{\'et}^{2d-3}(\overline{X}, \mathbb{Z}_\ell(d-1))/\ell^n \cap N^{d-2}H_\text{\'et}^{2d-3}(\overline{X}, \mathbb{Z}/\ell^n(d-1))\\
\xrightarrow{\phi} &\lim \limits_{\xleftarrow[n]{}} N^{d-2}H_\text{\'et}^{2d-3}(\overline{X}, \mathbb{Z}/\ell^n(d-1)) \to \lim \limits_{\xleftarrow[n]{}}H^{2d-2}_\text{\'et}(\overline{X}, \mathbb{Z}_\ell(d-1))[\ell^n],
\end{align*}
where the first inverse limit is $N^{d-2}H^{2d-3}_\text{\'et}(\overline{X}, \mathbb{Z}_\ell(d-1))$ by Claim \ref{claim:equal}, and the last inverse limit is torsion free.
Since the quotient
\[
H_\text{\'et}^{2d-3}(\overline{X}, \mathbb{Z}_\ell(d-1))/N^{d-2}H_\text{\'et}^{2d-3}(\overline{X}, \mathbb{Z}_\ell(d-1))
\]
is torsion by Corollary \ref{cor:2d-3torsion}, we know that $\phi$ is an isomorphism and thus 
\[
N^{d-2}H^{2d-3}_\text{\'et}(\overline{X}, \mathbb{Z}_\ell) \to H^{2d-3}_\text{\'et}(\overline{X}, \mathbb{Z}_\ell)
\]is an isomorphism.

By Theorem \ref{thm:image_sheaf}, the two subgroups $N^{d-2}H^{2d-3}_\text{\'et}(\overline{X}, \mathbb{Z}_\ell), \Tilde{N}^{d-2}H^{2d-3}_\text{\'et}(\overline{X}, \mathbb{Z}_\ell)$ agree. So they equal the whole cohomology group $H^{2d-3}_\text{\'et}(\overline{X}, \mathbb{Z}_\ell)$ by the previous paragraph. 
Then the corollary follows from \cite[Proposition 5.6]{ScaviaSuzuki2023coniveau}, the statement of which is recalled in Proposition \ref{thm:SS3}.

The $3$-fold case follows from Theorem \ref{thm:surj_dim3_chow}.

nodes.raw_latex:
\label{thm:TateImpiesCT}
Let $\mathbb{F}$ be a finite field, $C$ a smooth projective geometrically connected curve over $\mathbb{F}$, and $K$ the function field of $C$. 
Let $\mathcal{X}$ be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of dimension $d+1$ defined over $\mathbb{F}$, equipped with a morphism $p: \mathcal{X} \to C$, whose generic fiber $X$ is smooth and geometrically irreducible. Let $l$ be a prime different from the characteristic.
\begin{enumerate}
\item \label{itc1} If the cycle class map
\[
\text{CH}^d(\mathcal{X}) \otimes \mathbb{Z}_\ell \to H^{2d}_{\text{{\'e}t}}(\mathcal{X}, \mathbb{Z}_\ell(d))
\]
is surjective, Conjectures \ref{conj:CT1} and \ref{conj:CT2} are true for the generic fiber $X$.
\item \label{itc2} If the cycle class map
\[
\text{CH}^d(\mathcal{X}) \otimes \mathbb{Z}_\ell \to H^{2d}_{\text{{\'e}t}}(\mathcal{X}, \mathbb{Z}_\ell(d)) \to H^{2d}_{\text{{\'e}t}}(\overline{\mathcal{X}}, \mathbb{Z}_\ell(d))^G
\]
is surjective, or if 
\[
\text{CH}^d(\mathcal{X}) \otimes \mathbb{Z}_\ell \to H^{2d}_{\text{{\'e}t}}(\mathcal{X}, \mathbb{Z}_\ell(d))
\]
is surjective modulo torsion,
Conjecture \ref{conj:CT2} is true for the generic fiber $X$. 
\end{enumerate}

Let X be a smooth projective geometrically connected variety of dimension d+1 defined over F, equipped with a morphism p: X to C, whose generic fiber X is smooth and geometrically irreducible. Let l be a prime different from the characteristic. item If the cycle class map \[ CH^d(X) otimes Z_ell to H^2d_\'et(X, Z_ell(d)) \] is surjective, Conjectures and are true for the generic fiber X. item If the cycle class map \[ CH^d(X) otimes Z_ell to H^2d_\'et(X, Z_ell(d)) to H^2d_\'et(overlineX, Z_ell(d))^G \] is surjective, or if \[ CH^d(X) otimes Z_ell to H^2d_\'et(X, Z_ell(d)) \] is surjective modulo torsion, Conjecture is true for the generic fiber X.

Question \ref{q:CH0} has a positive answer if $X$ is a geometrically rational surface, and has a regular model with SNC central fiber (\cite[Theorem 3.1]{WittenbergEsnault_0_cycle} in general and \cite[Theorem A]{Saito_torsion_codim_2} for the case of $p$-adic fields without requiring having SNC central fiber).

This follows from computations in \cite{WittenbergEsnault_0_cycle}, discussed in the first paragraph of Section 4.3 of the paper. 
    
More precisely, in the course of the proving Theorems 3.1 and 4.1 of \cite{WittenbergEsnault_0_cycle}, Esnault and Wittenberg have shown that, under the hypothesis of the lemma, certain complex ((4.6) op. cit.) is injective, which, by an argument similar to Section 2.2 op. cit., turns out to be equivalent to the surjectivity of the cycle class map ((4.7) op. cit.):
\[
\text{CH}_1(A) \hat{\otimes}\mathbb{Z}_\ell \to H^{4}_A(\mathfrak{X}, \mathbb{Z}_\ell(2)).
\]
 Denote by $\{A_i, i\in I\}$ the set of reduced irreducible components of $A$. Each $A_i$ is a smooth projective surface.
Thus $A_1(A_i)$ is finitely generated (Theorem of the base \cite[XIII Th\'eor\`eme 5.1]{SGA6}).
Therefore the natural map $$\text{CH}_1(A_i)\otimes \mathbb{Z}_\ell \to A_1(A_i) \otimes \mathbb{Z}_\ell \cong A_1(A_i)\hat{\otimes}\mathbb{Z}_\ell\cong \text{CH}_1(A_i)\hat{\otimes} \mathbb{Z}_\ell$$ is surjective, where the last equality holds because $\text{CH}_1(A_i)_\text{alg}$ is divisible.
We also have a surjection $\oplus \text{CH}_1(A_i)/\ell^m \to \text{CH}_1(A)/\ell^m$. Since $\oplus \text{CH}_1(A_i)/\ell^m$ is a finite group, the Mittag-Leffler condition is satisfied and we have a surjection $\oplus \text{CH}_1(A_i)\hat{\otimes} \mathbb{Z}_\ell \to \text{CH}_1(A) \hat{\otimes} \mathbb{Z}_\ell$ after taking the inverse limit.
Therefore the $\ell$-adic cycle class map
\[
\oplus \text{CH}_1(A_i)\otimes \mathbb{Z}_\ell \to \text{CH}_1(A) \hat{\otimes}\mathbb{Z}_\ell \to H^{4}_A(\mathfrak{X}, \mathbb{Z}_\ell(2))
\]
is surjective. 
Since the above map factors through $\text{CH}_1(A) {\otimes}\mathbb{Z}_\ell$, the $\ell$-adic cycle class map
\[
\text{CH}_1(A) {\otimes}\mathbb{Z}_\ell \to H^{4}_A(\mathfrak{X}, \mathbb{Z}_\ell(2)).
\]
is surjective.

We have a canonical isomorphism
\[
H_2^{\text{BM}}(A, \mathbb{Z}/\ell^m(1)) \cong H^{4}_A(\mathfrak{X}, \mathbb{Z}/\ell^m(2)).
\]
To prove this isomorphism, consider the following commutative diagram:
\[

 Taking inverse limit, we have an isomorphism

So using resolution of singularities for $3$-folds \cite{Resolution1, Resolution2, AbhyankarResolution}, we may assume that the singular fibers are SNC divisors.

We take $\cup \mathcal{X}_i$ to be a non-empty finite union of fibers that contains all the singular fibers of the fibration $\mathcal{X} \to B$ and $\mathcal{X}^0$ its complement.
We have a commutative diagram of localization exact sequences, where the horizontal maps are localization sequences for Chow groups \cite[Proposition 1.8]{Fulton98} (resp. \'etale Borel-Moore homology) applied to the triple $(\overline{\mathcal{X}}, \cup \overline{\mathcal{X}}_{i, \text{red}}, \overline{\mathcal{X}}^0)$ (where $\overline{\mathcal{X}}_{i, \text{red}}$ means the reduced closed subscheme of $\overline{\mathcal{X}}_{i}$ ), and the vertical maps are cycle class maps for Chow groups:
\begin{equation}\label{eq:loc}
    \begin{CD}
 \oplus \text{CH}_1(\overline{\mathcal{X}}_{i, \text{red}})\otimes \mathbb{Z}_\ell @>>> \text{CH}_1(\overline{\mathcal{X}})\otimes \mathbb{Z}_\ell @>>>\text{CH}_1 (\overline{\mathcal{X}}^0)\otimes \mathbb{Z}_\ell @>>> 0 \\
@VVV @VVV @VVV\\
\oplus H_{2}^{\text{BM}}(\overline{\mathcal{X}}_{i, \text{red}}, \mathbb{Z}_\ell(1)) @>>>H_2^{\text{BM}}(\overline{\mathcal{X}}, \mathbb{Z}_\ell(1))@>>>H_2^{\text{BM}}(\overline{\mathcal{X}}^0, \mathbb{Z}_\ell(1))\\
\end{CD}
\end{equation}
  The commutativity of the left square follows from functoriality of Borel-Moore homology under proper push-forward. The commutativity of the right square follows from the fact that fundamental class commutes with restriction to an open subset (See \cite[1.3.4, and Example 2.1]{BlochOgus} for the case of $\mathbb{Z}/\ell^m$-coefficient. The $\mathbb{Z}_\ell$-coefficient case follows by taking inverse limit).


We apply Lemma \ref{lem:surj_fiber} in our situation. 
For each fiber $\overline{\mathcal{X}}_i$ over a point $b_i \in B(\bar{\mathbb{F}}_q)$, we base change $\overline{\mathcal{X}} \to \bar{B}$ to ${\mathfrak{X}}_i \to \text{Spec } \mathcal{O}_{\bar{B}, b_i}^{\text{h}}$, where $\mathcal{O}_{B, b_i}^{\text{h}}$ is the henselization of the local ring $\mathcal{O}_{\bar{B}, b_i}$ at $b_i$. Still denote by $\overline{\mathcal{X}}_i$ the closed fiber of $\mathfrak{X}_i$.
The $\ell$-adic cycle class map
\[
\text{CH}_1(\overline{\mathcal{X}}_{i, \text{red}})\otimes \mathbb{Z}_\ell \to H_2^{\text{BM}}(\overline{\mathcal{X}}_{i, \text{red}}, \mathbb{Z}_\ell(1))
\]
is surjective by Lemma \ref{lem:surj_fiber}.

Since we assume that the union $\cup \mathcal{X}_i$ is non-empty, the open complement $\overline{\mathcal{X}}^0$ is over an affine curve $B^0\subset B$.
By Lemma \ref{lem:H2d},
the cycle class of a section generates the group $ H_2^{\text{BM}}(\overline{\mathcal{X}}^0, \mathbb{Z}_\ell(1))\cong H^0(B^0,\mathcal{H}^4)\cong \mathbb{Z}_\ell$, and
thus the right vertical cycle class map in the commutative diagram (\ref{eq:loc}) is surjective.
So the middle map in the commutative diagram (\ref{eq:loc}) is also surjective.
This proves that hypothesis (A) in Theorem \ref{thm:integralTate} is satisfied.

The result of Bloch-Srinivas \cite[Theorem 1, (iii)]{BlochSrinivas} shows that the Griffiths group of one-cycles on $\overline{\mathcal{X}}$ is $p$-torsion (since for $\overline{\mathcal{X}}$ the rational Chow group of zero-cycles is universally supported on a curve by Corollary \ref{rem:support}). So hypothesis (B) in Theorem \ref{thm:integralTate} is satisfied.

Hypotheses (C) and (D) in Theorem \ref{thm:integralTate} are also satisfied in this case by Lemma \ref{3fold}.

The Hochschild-Serre spectral sequence gives a short exact sequence:
\[
0 \to H^1(\mathbb{F}_q, H^{2d-2r-1}_\text{\'et}(\overline{X}, \mathbb{Z}_\ell(d-r))) \to H^{2d-2r}_\text{\'et}(X, \mathbb{Z}_\ell(d-r)) \to H^{2d-2r}_\text{\'et}(\overline{X}, \mathbb{Z}_\ell(d-r))^G \to 0,
\]
where $G$ is the absolute Galois group of $\overline{\mathbb{F}}_q/\mathbb{F}_q$.
Thus Theorem \ref{thm:integralTate} implies that $\text{CH}_1(\mathcal{X}) \otimes \mathbb{Z}_\ell \to H^4(\mathcal{X}, \mathbb{Z}_l(2))$ is surjective.

Moreover, Sigma_1cap Sigma_2=sigma_0 is a common section of both ruled surfaces. And Sigma_1cup_sigma_0 Sigma_2 subset X is a family of chains of two lines connecting sigma_1, sigma_2. By previous argument, [sigma_C] and [sigma_B] are rationally equivalent modulo lines in general fibers. We push forward this rational equivalence relation to X via p. Since p_*[sigma_C]=[C], p_*[sigma_B]=d[sigma_0], and the push-forward of lines in general fibers are still lines in general fibers, we prove the second statement. Let $H$ be the scheme parameterizing the space of chains of two lines passing through $\sigma_1$ and $\sigma_2$, that is, curves of the form $(L_1\cup L_2, x_0, x_1, x_2)$, where $L_1$ and $L_2$ are two lines in a fiber $\mathcal{X}_b, b \in B$ intersecting at a single point $x_0$, $x_1 \in L_1, x_2 \in L_2$ and $x_1=\sigma_1(b), x_2=\sigma_2(b)$. 
The morphism $H \to B$ is proper, because a degeneration of a chain of two lines is again a chain of two lines. 


    The space of chains of two lines passing through two points in a complete intersection of degree $d_1, \ldots, d_c$ in $\mathbb{P}^n$ is defined by equations of degree $1,1,2,2, \ldots, d_1-1, d_1-1, d_1, 1, 1, \ldots, d_2-1, d_2-1, d_2, \ldots, 1, 1, \ldots, d_c-1, d_c-1, d_c$ in $\mathbb{P}^n$ (see, for example, Lemma 3.4 in \cite{Pan_conic}).
    
The classical Tsen-Lang theorem applied to the generic fiber of $H \to B$ implies that there is a rational section $B \dashrightarrow H$. Since $B$ is a curve, we can extend this to a section.
This is equivalent to the following.
The family $\mathcal{X} \to B$ contains two ruled surfaces over $B$: $B \leftarrow \Sigma_1 \subset \mathcal{X}, B \leftarrow \Sigma_2 \subset \mathcal{X}$, such that $\sigma_1 \subset \Sigma_1$ (resp. $\sigma_2 \subset \Sigma_2$) is a section.
Moreover, $\Sigma_1\cap \Sigma_2=\sigma_0$ is a common section of both ruled surfaces. And $\Sigma_1\cup_{\sigma_0} \Sigma_2 \subset \mathcal{X}$ is a family of chains of two lines connecting $\sigma_1, \sigma_2$.

Any  two sections in a $\mathbb{P}^1$-bundle over a curve are rationally equivalent modulo general fibers.
Thus both $\sigma_1, \sigma_2$  are rationally equivalent to $\sigma_0$ up to lines in general fibers.
Pushing forward this rational equivalence to $\mathcal{X}$ proves the first statement.

Given $C\subset \mathcal{X}$ such that $C \to B$ is dominant of degree $d$, we make a base change $\mathcal{X}_C=\mathcal{X} \times_B C \xrightarrow{(p, q)} \mathcal{X} \times C$. 
The family $\mathcal{X}_C \to C$ admits two sections: $\sigma_C$, induced by the inclusion $C \subset \mathcal{X}$, and $\sigma_B$, induced by $C \to B \to \sigma_0 \subset \mathcal{X}$.
By previous argument, $[\sigma_C]$ and $[\sigma_B]$ are rationally equivalent modulo lines in general fibers.
We push forward this rational equivalence relation to $\mathcal{X}$ via $p$. Since $p_*[\sigma_C]=[C], p_*[\sigma_B]=d[\sigma_0]$, and the push-forward of lines in general fibers are still lines in general fibers, we prove the second statement.

Any curve in a fiber is rationally equivalent to the difference of two multi-sections of the same degree.
So it is also rationally equivalent to a sum of cycle class of lines in general fibers.

Finally, since the Fano scheme of lines of a complete intersection of degree $(d_1, \ldots, d_c)$ in $\mathbb{P}^n$ is connected as long as $2n-c-\sum d_i>2$ \cite[Th\'eor\`eme 2.1]{DebarreManivelFanoScheme}, all lines in the fibers are algebraically equivalent.
This proves the fourth statement.

Then the cycle class map \[ CH^d(X) otimes Z_ell to H^2d_\'et(X, Z_ell(d)) \] is surjective and Conjectures and hold for the generic fiber X over F_q(B).

\label{rem:bm_condition}
The numerical conditions imply that $X$ is either a quadric of dimension $3$ or has dimension at least $4$.
Thus the condition \ref{ci}.(2) on Borel-Moore homology holds for all smooth fibers by Lefschetz hyperplane theorem.
It also holds for singular fibers with ordinary double points.

By Theorem \ref{thm:integralTate} and  by Theorem \ref{thm:TateImpiesCT},
it suffices to show:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item $A_1(\overline{\mathcal{X}})\otimes \mathbb{Z}_\ell \cong H^{2d}(\overline{\mathcal{X}}, \mathbb{Z}_\ell(d)).$
    \item $N^{d-1}H^{2d-1}(\overline{\mathcal{X}}, \mathbb{Z}_\ell(d))  
=H^{2d-1}(\overline{\mathcal{X}}, \mathbb{Z}_\ell(d)).$
\end{enumerate}
There is an open subset $B^0 \subset \bar{B}$ such that $\mathcal{X}^0=\overline{\mathcal{X}}|_{B^0}$ is a complete intersection of ample divisors in $\mathbb{P}(E)|_{B^0}$.
In case \ref{ci}.(1), we take $B^0$ in such a way that $B\backslash B^0$ is a single point with smooth fiber.
In case \ref{ci}.(2), we take $B^0$ so that ${\mathcal{X}}^0 \to B^0$ is smooth.


Write $\mathcal{X}_0$ to be the disjoint union of all the fibers over $B\backslash B^0$.
Denote by $\mathbb{P}^0$ the open subscheme $\overline{\mathbb{P}_B(E)}|_{B^0}$, and $U^0$ the open subscheme $\mathbb{P}^0\backslash \mathcal{X}^0$.


We use the localization sequence of \'etale cohomology
\begin{align*}
   \ldots \to &H^{2d-1}_{\mathcal{X}_0}(\overline{\mathcal{X}}, \mathbb{Z}_\ell(d-1)) \to H^{2d-1}(\overline{\mathcal{X}}, \mathbb{Z}_\ell(d)) \to H^{2d-1}({\mathcal{X}}^0, \mathbb{Z}_\ell(d)) \\
    \to&H^{2d}_{\mathcal{X}_0}(\overline{\mathcal{X}}, \mathbb{Z}_\ell(d-1)) \to H^{2d}(\overline{\mathcal{X}}, \mathbb{Z}_\ell(d)) \to H^{2d}({\mathcal{X}}^0, \mathbb{Z}_\ell(d))\\ \to &H^{2d+1}(\mathcal{X}_0, \mathbb{Z}_\ell(d-1))\ldots,
\end{align*}
We have the isomorphisms \[
H^{2d-3}_{\mathcal{X}_0}(\overline{\mathcal{X}}, \mathbb{Z}_\ell(d-1))\cong H^\text{BM}_3(\mathcal{X}_0, \mathbb{Z}_\ell(1))=0,\]
\[
H^{2d-2}_{\mathcal{X}_0}(\overline{\mathcal{X}}, \mathbb{Z}_\ell(d-1))\cong \oplus_{b \in B\backslash B^0} H^{\text{BM}}_2(\mathcal{X}_b, \mathbb{Z}_\ell(1)) \cong \oplus_{b \in B\backslash B^0} \mathbb{Z}_\ell\cdot [L_b],\]
where $[L_b]$ is the class of a line in $\mathcal{X}_b$.
In the case where $X$ is a hypersurface,
the above isomorphisms follow from Remark \ref{rem:bm_condition} and standard facts about cohomology of smooth hypersurfaces.
In the case of complete intersections, the above isomorphisms follow from our assumption.

Moreover the map
\[
H^{2d-2}_{\mathcal{X}_0}(\overline{\mathcal{X}}, \mathbb{Z}_\ell(d-1)) \to H^{2d}(\overline{\mathcal{X}}, \mathbb{Z}_\ell(d))
\]
has one-dimensional image spanned by the class of a line in the total space by Lemma \ref{lem:multisection}, part (3) and (4).




In case \ref{ci}.(1), we use the following localization long exact sequence:
\begin{align*}
&H^{2d}(U^0, \mathbb{Z}_\ell(d+1))\to H^{2d-1}(\overline{\mathcal{X}}|_{B^0}, \mathbb{Z}_\ell(d)) \xrightarrow{\cong} H^{2d+1}(\mathbb{P}^0, \mathbb{Z}_\ell(d+1)) \\
    &H^{2d+1}(U^0, \mathbb{Z}_\ell(d+1))\to H^{2d}(\overline{\mathcal{X}}|_{B^0}, \mathbb{Z}_\ell(d)) \xrightarrow{\cong} H^{2d+2}(\mathbb{P}^0, \mathbb{Z}_\ell(d+1)) \\
    \to &H^{2d+2}(U^0, \mathbb{Z}_\ell(d+1))\ldots .
\end{align*}
The open complement $U^0$ is an affine variety of dimension $n+1$. Under our assumptions on $d$ and $n$, we have $2d=2n-2>n+1$.
So by Artin vanishing for \'etale cohomology, 
\[
H^{2d}(U^0, \mathbb{Z}_\ell(d+1))= H^{2d+1}(U^0, \mathbb{Z}_\ell(d+1))= H^{2d+2}(U^0, \mathbb{Z}_\ell(d+1))=0.
\]
Therefore we have isomorphisms
\[
H^{2d-1}(\overline{\mathcal{X}}|_{B^0}, \mathbb{Z}_\ell(d)) \xrightarrow{\cong} H^{2d+1}(\mathbb{P}^0, \mathbb{Z}_\ell(d+1)), \]
\[ H^{2d}(\overline{\mathcal{X}}|_{B^0}, \mathbb{Z}_\ell(d)) \xrightarrow{\cong} H^{2d+2}(\mathbb{P}^0, \mathbb{Z}_\ell(d+1)).
\]
We know that $H^{2d}(\mathbb{P}^0, \mathbb{Z}_\ell(d+1))$ is spanned by the class of a section by Lemma \ref{lem:H2d}, and that $H^{2d-1}(\mathbb{P}^0, \mathbb{Z}_\ell(d+1))$ is supported on a surface swept out by a family of lines by Lemma \ref{lem:sm_fil}.
Since we also have a section of $\overline{\mathcal{X}} \to B$ and we may choose the family of lines to lie in $\overline{\mathcal{X}}$, the same is true for $\mathcal{X}^0=\overline{\mathcal{X}}|_{B^0}$ in this case.


In case \ref{ci}.(2), the group $H^{2d}(\overline{\mathcal{X}}|_{B^0}, \mathbb{Z}_\ell(d))$ is spanned by the class of a section by Lemma \ref{lem:H2d}.
So $H^{2d}(\overline{\mathcal{X}}, \mathbb{Z}_\ell(d))$ is spanned by the class of a section and a line.
By Corollary \ref{cor:sm_fil}, our assumption on singular fibers also implies that $H^{2d-1}(\overline{\mathcal{X}}, \mathbb{Z}_\ell(d))$ is supported on a surface.


Over the algebraic closure $\overline{\mathbb{F}}_q$,  by Lemma \ref{lem:multisection}, the group $A_1(\overline{\mathcal{X}})$ is a free abelian group of rank $2$, generated by the class of a section and a line in a general fiber.
As a result, \[
A_1(\overline{\mathcal{X}})\otimes \mathbb{Z}_\ell \cong H^{2d}_\text{\'et}(\overline{\mathcal{X}}, \mathbb{Z}_\ell(d)).\]
This concludes the proof.

So by Artin vanishing for \'etale cohomology, \[ H^2d(U^0, Z_ell(d+1))= H^2d+1(U^0, Z_ell(d+1))= H^2d+2(U^0, Z_ell(d+1))=0. \] Therefore we have isomorphisms \[ H^2d-1(overlineX|_B^0, Z_ell(d)) xrightarrowcong H^2d+1(P^0, Z_ell(d+1)), \] \[ H^2d(overlineX|_B^0, Z_ell(d)) xrightarrowcong H^2d+2(P^0, Z_ell(d+1)). \] We know that H^2d(P^0, Z_ell(d+1)) is spanned by the class of a section by Lemma , and that H^2d-1(P^0, Z_ell(d+1)) is supported on a surface swept out by a family of lines by Lemma . Since we also have a section of overlineX to B and we may choose the family of lines to lie in overlineX, the same is true for X^0=overlineX|_B^0 in this case. In case .(2), the group H^2d(overlineX|_B^0, Z_ell(d)) is spanned by the class of a section by Lemma . So H^2d(overlineX, Z_ell(d)) is spanned by the class of a section and a line. By Corollary , our assumption on singular fibers also implies that H^2d-1(overlineX, Z_ell(d)) is supported on a surface. Over the algebraic closure overlineF_q, by Lemma , the group A_1(overlineX) is a free abelian group of rank 2, generated by the class of a section and a line in a general fiber. As a result, \[ A_1(overlineX)otimes Z_ell cong H^2d_\'et(overlineX, Z_ell(d)).\] This concludes the proof.

By the work of Saito-Sato \cite[Theorem 1.16]{SaitoSato_0_cycle}, if $X$ admits a regular model $\mathfrak{X} \to \text{Spec } R$ such that the cental fiber is a simple normal crossing (SNC) divisor, the cycle class map induces an isomorphism 
\[
\text{CH}^d(\mathfrak{X})/\ell^n \xrightarrow{\cong} H^{2d}_\text{\'et}(\mathfrak{X}, \mu_{\ell^n}),
\]
where $d$ the the dimension of $X$.
We have the following commutative diagram of localization sequences for Chow groups and \'etale cohomology:
\[
\begin{CD}
    \text{CH}^{d-1}(\mathfrak{X}_0)/\ell^n @>>> \text{CH}^d(\mathfrak{X})/\ell^n @>>> \text{CH}^d(X)/\ell^n \to 0\\
    @VVV @VV\cong V @VVV\\
    H^{2d}_{\mathfrak{X}_0}(\mathfrak{X}, \mu_{\ell^n}^{\otimes d})@>>>H^{2d}(\mathfrak{X}, \mu_{\ell^n}^{\otimes d})@>>> H^{2d}(X, \mu_{\ell^n}^{\otimes d}),
\end{CD}
\]
where the left vertical map maybe identified with the cycle class map to the Borel-Moore homology
\[
\text{CH}_1(\mathfrak{X}_0)/\ell^n \to H_2^{\text{BM}}(\mathfrak{X}_0, \mu_{\ell^n}).
\]
